about: POST /oid4vp/call and GET /oid4vp/limits (api/oid4vp_proxy.js), added by #436 after the data model was recorded (#437). The refusals and the limits document were computed from api/oid4vp_proxy.js with api/env/docker-tests.js, the configuration the containerized stack runs; every outbound target is verifier.invalid, so no case leaves the api. The Verifier role's nine routes (api/oid4vp_verifier.js, #364) were added with their model: a session's id and secret are generated, so the cases that reach one by id use one that was never created (every page call there is a 404 before its Bearer secret is asked for), and the one session created here asks for a 1 ms idle lifetime, so it is gone by the next request and replaying this file never reaches oid4vpVerifierMaxSessionsPerCaller. The live-signing publish (oid4vpVerifierPublishFor) needs a Wallet held open on a live session, which no single recorded request can make, so its cases are the unknown session and the wrong type; the held Wallet, the 401s, the timeout, and the 503 temporarily_unavailable (oid4vpVerifierRequestPost) that a Wallet which sent a wallet_nonce gets on a timeout or at oid4vpVerifierMaxPendingSignings (OpenID4VP section 5.10.2) are driven by tests/api_oid4vp_verifier.js too. The lifecycle, the 401s, the media types and the size caps are driven by tests/api_oid4vp_verifier.js. #470 (B3) added responseEncoding to the call; its refusals are recorded here. #470 (B5) added publicBaseUrl to create and to the Verifier limits; its refusals are recorded here, and a create with a publicBaseUrl, whose URLs are generated, is driven by tests/api_oid4vp_verifier.js. #471 (E4) lets the live-signing publish carry a compact JWE, the Request Object signed then encrypted to a key from the Wallet's wallet_metadata (RFC 9101 section 4); the model takes it as a string like the JWS, and its case here is the unknown session. A held Wallet receiving one is driven by tests/api_oid4vp_verifier.js.

cases.name: oid4vp call: an empty body is refused for its url

body.error: url is required: the request_uri, the response_uri, or the redirect_uri a SIOPv2 post goes to, exactly as the Verifier named it.

cases.name: oid4vp call: a url that is not http(s) is refused

body.error: url must be an absolute http:// or https:// URL. OpenID4VP names every endpoint absolutely, and a relative one resolved against this service would reach the api's own routes.

cases.name: oid4vp call: a method other than GET or POST is refused

body.error: method must be GET or POST. A wallet fetches a Request Object and posts an answer, and nothing else crosses in OpenID4VP; another method would make this endpoint useful for something that is not a presentation.

cases.name: oid4vp call: a body that is not a string is refused

body.error: body must be a string: OpenID4VP's bodies are application/x-www-form-urlencoded, and the page sends them encoded exactly as they are to travel.

cases.name: oid4vp call: a GET carrying a body is refused

body.error: A GET carries no body. Fetching a Request Object by POST is request_uri_method=post, and is sent as a POST; a body silently dropped from a GET is how the wrong method goes unnoticed.

cases.name: oid4vp call: a responseEncoding other than text or base64 is refused

body.error: responseEncoding must be "text" or "base64": the body comes back as the text that arrived, or as its bytes in base64 (a status list may be binary CBOR).

cases.name: oid4vp call: a responseEncoding that is not a string

body.error: Refusing the request: `responseEncoding` must be a JSON string or null. GET /api-docs describes what oid4vpCall takes.

cases.name: oid4vp call: a framing header is refused

body.error: This endpoint will not forward the Content-Length header. The body framing is this service's to set — a caller that could set it could smuggle a second request inside the first. Everything else is forwarded as sent — the refusals here are about the SHAPE of the request rather than its content.

cases.changed: #470 (B3) added responseEncodings: the Verifier page's issuer, DID and status list fetches come back as base64 bytes, because a status list may be a binary CWT.

body.statusRule: a 400 is this service refusing; a 502 is the Verifier unreachable; anything the Verifier answered is a 200 with its status inside.

cases.name: verifier limits: what the Verifier role will hold
cases.changed: Live signing (#364, request_uri_method=post) added liveSignWaitMs and maxPendingSignings. #470 (B5) then added publicBaseUrl (oid4vpVerifierPublicBaseUrl, empty here); `before` is the answer from before that second change.

body.note: A page cannot be an HTTP server, so it cannot be the request_uri or the response_uri a Wallet connects to. This service hosts both on the page's behalf: the page signs the Request Object itself and publishes it here, and reads back what Wallets posted. Nothing is verified here; the page verifies.

cases.name: verifier create: a redirectUri that is not a string

body.error: Refusing the request: `redirectUri` must be a JSON string or null. GET /api-docs describes what oid4vpVerifierCreate takes.

cases.name: verifier create: a ttlMs that is not a number is refused

body.error: ttlMs must be a positive whole number of milliseconds; it was "soon". Leave it out for the default (oid4vpVerifierTtlMs, 1800000).

cases.name: verifier create: a ttlMs above the ceiling is refused

body.error: ttlMs 999999999 is above this service's ceiling, oid4vpVerifierTtlMs = 1800000. A page may ask for less, never more.

cases.name: verifier create: a redirectUri with a line break is refused

body.error: redirectUri may not contain a line break.

cases.name: verifier create: a liveSigning that is not a boolean

body.error: Refusing the request: `liveSigning` must be a JSON boolean or null. GET /api-docs describes what oid4vpVerifierCreate takes.

cases.name: verifier create: a publicBaseUrl that is not https is refused

body.error: publicBaseUrl must be an https:// URL: a Wallet fetches request_uri and posts to response_uri over TLS. It was "http://verifier.invalid:4000".

body.error: Refusing the request: `publicBaseUrl` must be a JSON string or null. GET /api-docs describes what oid4vpVerifierCreate takes.
